true_answer: e cyclical view of time contrasts with the linear concept of time more common in Western thought, where time is seen as progressing in a straight line from past to future without repetition.[49] In general, the Islamic and Judeo-Christian world-view regards time as linear[50] and directional,[51] beginning with the act of creation by God. e traditional Christian view sees time ending, teleologically,[52] with the eschatological end of the present order of things, the 'end time'.
